name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Translate information hierarchy into containers

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Map records, groups, selection and supporting detail before choosing lists, collections, split views, tabs or disclosure. Open the procedure for the candidate container.
2. Separate grouping from navigation: a box organizes related content; a split view coordinates hierarchical panes; disclosure reveals optional detail. Do not use a container merely because space is available.
3. For resizing, large content and empty states, retain a coherent selection and route back. Identify minimum useful pane/content behavior from the task rather than fixed screenshots.
4. Deliver the hierarchy, selection model, adaptive layout decisions and a patch or verification matrix covering narrow and expanded states.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

name: apple-hig-tab-views
description: Use when choosing, reviewing, or adapting mutually exclusive related content panes within a shared view.

# Keep pane switching distinct from app navigation

Read [the tab-view guide](../../references/tab-views.md). This procedure is application advice; distinguish the conventional Mac pane control from top-level tab bars and framework names.

Inspect the pane contents, affected controls, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Determine whether the choices are self-contained related views or unrelated app destinations. Count meaningful choices, record their labels, and identify any action that affects another pane.

Use tabs for a small set of related panes, with short predictive labels and controls scoped to their pane. Keep the tab control visible unless switching is programmatic; otherwise people lose the route among choices. Evaluate another presentation already at six or more choices rather than squeezing a growing category list. Normally inset the content within window margins. Conventional pane-style tabs belong to macOS; evaluate segmented controls on iOS/iPadOS, appropriate navigation elsewhere, and page behavior for watch SwiftUI tab views. Do not equate every `TabView` API with the Mac component.

Implement the pane switch, produce a pane/control ownership specification, or review specific category/scope defects. Preserve the intended state of each pane when changing views, documenting that application choice rather than assuming automatic persistence.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a Mac audio inspector has nine tabs and a gain control in “Metadata” that unexpectedly changes “Mix.” Decision: choice count and cross-pane scope obscure the model. After: group related inspector content into fewer coherent panes or a view-choice pop-up, and place gain with the mix controls it affects.

Deliver the artifact, labels, ownership, and switching/state policy. Verify every choice is reachable, labels fit localization, and controls affect only their documented scope. Fail for hidden user-driven navigation, misclassified app destinations, or effects in an unrelated pane. Report native page/Crown behavior only when exercised.

Use [tab-bars](../../../apple-hig-navigation-and-search/.topics/apple-hig-tab-bars/SKILL.md) for top-level navigation or [segmented-controls](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-segmented-controls/SKILL.md) for a supported related-view switch.

name: apple-hig-settings
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting app-wide configuration, task-local options, system preferences, and settings access or persistence.

# Put an option where its effect is understood

Read [the settings guide](../../references/settings.md). This workflow is application advice; platform locations and system preference scope constrain the design.

Inspect option inventory/frequency, affected scope, defaults, system counterparts, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Classify task-local, document-wide, app-wide, and system-wide choices. Record actual capability detection/persistence rather than treating a displayed toggle as proof.

Choose sensible defaults and detect capabilities instead of asking for information already known. Keep frequent view/task options beside their visible effect and rare app-wide choices in settings. Do not duplicate system accessibility/authentication/scrolling preferences with misleading scope. Reserve system Settings entries for rare changes. On Mac place app Settings in the app menu with expected access, document setup in File, and use stable settings-pane navigation/title/restoration rather than a customizable main toolbar. Watch cannot add custom entries to system Settings; keep only essential in-app options. Preserve familiar game access where appropriate.

Implement option placement/persistence or provide a scope/default/location contract; reviews identify exact misplaced or contradictory settings. Do not expand a settings redesign into unauthorized global configuration changes.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a Mac map app puts its layer filter in app Settings and a global Reduce Motion copy in the main toolbar, while document scale changes every map. Decision: frequency and scope are inverted. After: keep layers local, respect system motion preference, and separate document scale from app-wide defaults.

Deliver the artifact, option scope, defaults/detection, access, and restoration policy. Verify default/changed values, reopen/last pane, per-document independence, and capability changes. Fail for misleading global/local scope, duplicated conflicting system preference, or lost expected settings access. Native settings/shortcut behavior requires execution evidence.

Load [the-menu-bar](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-the-menu-bar/SKILL.md), [toggles](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-toggles/SKILL.md), or [onboarding](../apple-hig-onboarding/SKILL.md) for access, state controls, or deferred setup.

name: apple-hig-entering-data
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting data-entry flows, known defaults, required fields, validation, and efficient input alternatives.

# Ask only for information the task still needs

Read [the data-entry guide](../../references/entering-data.md). This workflow is application advice; permission and authentication remain distinct from cosmetic entry behavior.

Inspect required information, existing system/account data, sensitivity, constraints, platform/input, and create/review/adapt intent. Identify redundant questions, reasonable nonsecret defaults, and information requiring permission. Record actual validation/gating behavior rather than assuming disabled Continue explains itself.

Reuse known appropriate data or request relevant permission; never prepopulate passwords. Prefer meaningful choices over typing and allow appropriate paste/drop. Keep persistent purpose labels, secure sensitive entry, and locale-aware numeric formatting. Validate while mistakes can be fixed in context without rejecting harmless intermediate entry. Make missing requirements understandable before gating Next/Continue. On Mac expansion tooltips can reveal clipped values; on visionOS secure entry protects AirPlay viewing according to the source, but do not claim arbitrary mirrored content is private.

Implement the authorized flow, provide a field/data-source/validation/gating specification, or review exact effort/error defects. Keep the user's task and stack rather than turning ordinary entry into an unsolicited account overhaul.

**Worked transformation:** Before: an expense form asks for known currency twice, prefills a stored password, blocks paste into the receipt ID, and disables Continue without explanation. Decision: defaults and friction are misapplied. After: reuse a suitable currency default, request secure authentication explicitly, permit useful paste, and identify the specific missing required input.

Deliver the artifact, requested versus reused data, input alternatives, and validation/continuation contract. Verify partial/invalid/valid values, locale, paste, sensitive fields, and the reason for gating. Fail for exposed secrets, unnecessary re-entry, valid input silently changed, or unexplained dead-end completion. Separate static/form logic from native input/permission/device execution.

Load [text-fields](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-text-fields/SKILL.md), [virtual-keyboards](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-virtual-keyboards/SKILL.md), or [privacy](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) as needed.

# Tab views Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-views) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A tab view swaps mutually exclusive, related panes within a shared content area. This article's pane-switching component is distinct from an app's top-level tab bar. ## Best practices Keep panes closely related and self-contained: controls inside one pane affect that pane. Label tabs to predict their contents, generally with short nouns or noun phrases in title case; a short action phrase can suit some contexts. A visible tab control exposes choices and takes one activation, whereas a pop-up hides choices and takes two. Avoid exceeding six tabs; already at six or more, evaluate a different presentation such as a pop-up containing view choices. ## Anatomy The tab control normally sits on the top edge of the content. Hide it only when the app switches panes programmatically. Without visible tabs, the content can have a bezel, a line border, or no border; borderless content can be opaque or transparent. Normally inset the whole view with window-body margins on every side, leaving room for unrelated controls. Extending it to the window edge is possible but unusual. ## Platform considerations The conventional tab-view component is unsupported in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, and visionOS; macOS supplies the pane-style control. ### iOS, iPadOS Evaluate a segmented control for a similar switch among related views. ### watchOS SwiftUI tab views use page controls. The indicator beside the Digital Crown identifies pages and can enlarge the active dot to show that its content can scroll as well as move between pages. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Tab bars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-bars) [Segmented controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/segmented-controls) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 5, 2023.

# Settings Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Use sensible defaults and respect system preferences. App-wide configuration, task-local controls, and system Settings belong in different places according to how often and where people need them. ## Best practices Optimize defaults for most people and automatically detect capabilities such as connected controllers or appearance. Keep the settings set small. Support expected access, including Command-Comma and game Escape. Do not duplicate systemwide accessibility, scrolling, or authentication settings in a way that suggests they have different scope. ## General settings Put infrequently changed experience-wide choices, such as window configuration, saving behavior, key mappings, or account preferences, in the app's settings area. ## Task-specific options Expose frequent view/task changes where their effects are visible: filtering, reordering, and showing/hiding content. In games, approach to a current challenge normally belongs to gameplay rather than a settings trip. ## System settings Reserve system-app entries for the rarest changes and, where useful, link directly from the app. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### macOS Place Settings in the app menu, not the main toolbar; document-level configuration belongs in File. A settings window can use a stable noncustomizable always-visible pane toolbar with active selection. Dim minimize/zoom because reopening is easy and size follows the pane. Use the current pane as title, or App Name Settings for one pane, and restore the previously visited pane. ### watchOS Apps do not add custom entries to system Settings. Offer only essential options, perhaps at the main view's bottom or through More for object configuration. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Onboarding](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — Foundation ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 10, 2024.

# Entering data Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/entering-data) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Reduce effort and mistakes by gathering known information and supporting the input methods available to the person. ## Best practices Get existing system/settings data automatically or request permission for relevant private data. Clearly label requested information and prefill reasonable nonsecret defaults. Securely obscure sensitive text or TV digit entry; visionOS secure fields keep input private from AirPlay viewers. Never prepopulate passwords: use explicit entry, biometrics, or keychain authentication. Prefer meaningful choices to typing, and accept paste and drag/drop where appropriate. Validate early enough to fix mistakes in context, with locale-aware number formatting for numeric constraints/presentation. Make required-data gating understandable, enabling Next/Continue only when necessary information is supplied. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS rules are specified. ### macOS An expansion tooltip can expose complete clipped/truncated field content on pointer dwell, including for iOS/iPadOS apps running on Mac. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Text fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-fields) [Virtual keyboards](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/virtual-keyboards) [Keyboards](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 21, 2023.

# Choose one state without hiding its meaning

Read [the pop-up-button guide](../../references/pop-up-buttons.md). This procedure is application advice; distinguish selection from command execution.

Inspect the option set, current/default value, label, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Establish whether the list is flat and mutually exclusive. If it contains commands, multiple selection, or submenus, evaluate a pull-down instead. Record actual selected value from data, not solely a possibly stale button title.

Use a pop-up when space is limited and options need not remain exposed. Give the control or nearby introduction a predictive purpose; start with a useful likely default when appropriate. After choosing, close the menu and reflect the value. A rare Custom option can open less-common choices; define how cancellation retains the prior value so entering customization does not imply commitment. On iPad, a small well-defined set may replace unnecessary detail navigation inside a modal/popover. Do not prescribe the component on tvOS/watchOS.

Implement the selection model, provide a label/options/default/commit specification, or review concrete mismatches. Keep value persistence and preview effects explicit rather than assuming a framework's automatic behavior.

**Worked transformation:** Before: `Options` mixes `Portrait`, `Landscape`, and `Print Now`, with no selected state. Decision: orientation is one persistent choice while printing is an action. After: a labelled Orientation pop-up displays the selected orientation; Print becomes a separate direct command.

Deliver the artifact and selection/customization contract. Verify default, repeated selection, external value change, cancellation of Custom, and long labels. Fail for a displayed value differing from stored state, hidden command disguised as a choice, or ambiguous list purpose. State native keyboard/assistive selection checks separately.

# Preserve context without multiplying clutter

Read [the window guide](../../references/windows.md). This workflow is application advice for the supported multiwindow platforms, not a claim that every OS has identical windows.

Inspect document/task identity, current windows, parallel-work needs, size ranges, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Distinguish a primary workspace from a short auxiliary task and a context-following panel. Record open/reuse/close behavior and main/key ownership from evidence; a screenshot does not establish window identity.

Open another window when preserving context or parallel work helps, with explicit Open in New Window where useful; avoid clutter by default. Retain system frames/movement/resize/close controls and call them windows in product copy. Set useful size constraints and adapt between them. On iPad protect leading tools from window controls and support the chosen fullscreen/windowed context. On Mac preserve key/main/inactive cues and normal movement/minimization; avoid critical bottom controls potentially offscreen.

For visionOS choose familiar glass windows for familiar tasks, shallow depth near their surface, and volumes for deeper multi-angle objects. Preserve glass legibility/grouping unless the requested content justifies another supported style. For volumes choose true-scale versus dynamic scaling intentionally, appropriate alignment, viewer-relative attachments, and bounded ornament placement. Do not prescribe the multiwindow component on iOS/tvOS/watchOS.

Implement window identity/adaptation, specify open/reuse/size/ownership behavior, or review concrete clutter/context defects. Do not infer physical size comfort or clipping from Linux rendering.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a spatial model viewer removes window glass, places a deep model outside its clipped surface, and opens a fresh window for every property click. Decision: depth and UI context require different containers. After: keep property tools in the existing window/split context and put the deep model in a suitable volume with bounded attachments and deliberate scaling.

Deliver the artifact and window/container lifecycle, sizing, and context contract. Verify repeated opens, multiple documents, resize extremes, close/reopen, and activation state. Fail for wrong-object reuse, unreachable controls, lost task context, or deeper content clipped by the selected container. Separate static/runtime checks from native window management and spatial-device validation.

# Pop-up buttons Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pop-up-buttons) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A pop-up button offers one choice from a flat list, then closes its menu and can display the selection. ## Best practices Use it for mutually exclusive states or options. Use a pull-down when the list contains actions, multiple selections, or submenus. Start with a useful default, usually a likely choice. Let a button or introductory label explain the hidden list's purpose. This is efficient where space is limited and options need not remain visible. An occasional Custom option can open less-common choices without crowding the default interface; explanatory text can clarify the list if needed. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, macOS, or visionOS rules are specified. Pop-up buttons are unsupported in tvOS and watchOS. ### iPadOS Inside a modal or popover, a pop-up can replace navigation through a row disclosure when a small well-defined option set fits a menu, avoiding a needless detail view. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Pull-down buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pull-down-buttons) [Buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons) [Menus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/menus) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: October 24, 2023, September 14, 2022.

# Windows Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/windows) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Primary windows host app navigation, content, and actions. Auxiliary windows focus on one task or area and typically close after that task. iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS windows establish content boundaries and enable multitasking with system movement, sizing, and closing controls. ## Best practices Adapt smoothly to size changes. Open new windows when preserving context or working in parallel helps, without generating clutter by default. Offer Open in New Window in a context or File menu when useful. Retain system frames and controls instead of imitating them. Call the experience a window in user-facing copy; scene is an implementation term. ## Platform considerations This multiwindow component guidance marks iOS, tvOS, and watchOS unsupported. ### iPadOS People choose fullscreen or windowed behavior in Multitasking & Gestures settings. Fullscreen fills the display and uses app switching; windowed mode supports multiple resizable, movable windows with remembered placement. Move leading toolbar items inward when window controls appear so they do not overlap. Consider gestures to open content in a new window, such as expanding a collection item with a pinch. Quick Look can present a single file without a custom window if the app supports multiple windows. ### macOS Support normal movement, resize, minimization, and frequent switching among multiple apps' windows. Games also need the appropriate system game-window configuration. #### macOS window anatomy A frame above the body supplies movement, window controls, and optionally a toolbar. Edges normally resize. A rare bottom bar is also part of the frame. #### macOS window states An app has one main window; the system has one key/input window at a time. A floating panel can be key while its document stays main. Dock activation brings app windows forward but makes only the recently used one key. Other windows are inactive. Colored close/minimize/zoom controls identify key state; inactive and non-key main windows use gray, and inactive windows lose vibrancy. Some panels take key status only through the title bar or keyboard-input controls. Custom rendering must preserve these automatic state cues. Avoid critical controls at the bottom, which may be offscreen; reserve bottom bars for small contextual summaries, using an inspector for more detail. ### visionOS Windows and volumetric windows can each contain 2D/3D content and coexist in Shared or Full Space. Plain style omits the glass plane. The system positions the first opened surface, then people can move it. #### visionOS windows Default windows use an upright glass plane with close, move, and resize controls, and can add Share, tabs, toolbars, and ornaments. Dynamic scale preserves apparent size across distance. Prefer familiar windows for familiar tasks, reserving immersion for meaningful content. Retain the glass background: it adapts to surroundings and communicates scale and position; removing it weakens legibility and grouping, while an opaque replacement conceals surroundings. Default initial size is 1280×720 pt, placed about 2 meters ahead with an apparent width of about 3 meters. Avoid excess empty space and choose a shape suited to content. Set minimum/maximum sizes and adapt layout throughout. Keep 3D depth shallow in a window because content too far from its surface is clipped; use a volume for deeper objects. #### visionOS volumes Volumes show bounded content from multiple angles; close and move controls turn to face the viewer. Prefer them for rich 3D scenes over UI-centric interfaces. Pin 2D overlays to 3D content with attachments and test multiple viewpoints. Dynamic scaling usually improves distant legibility and interaction, but fixed scaling (the default) suits true-to-life products. From visionOS 2, a baseplate border glow on look reveals bounds and resize controls when content does not fill them. Full-bleed content or a custom baseplate may not need it. Volumes can have an ornament alongside toolbar/tabs: use attachment anchors to keep its position viewer-relative, place it on another edge, and usually add only one. Choose a floor-parallel alignment for largely viewed objects, or a viewer-tilting alignment when interactive content should remain usable while reclining. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) [Split views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/split-views) [Multitasking](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/multitasking) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 9, 2025, June 10, 2024, June 21, 2023.

# Revised Mac preferences interaction specification

## Basis and decisions

"'`interface.md` supplies macOS, nine icon-only tabs with duplicate icons, unrelated file saves on selection, large size changes that displace Close, and unspecified validation errors. It supplies no pane names, option inventory, code, or screenshots. Treat these as reported behavior, not independently reproduced results.

1. **Replace the nine-tab strip with one labeled pane-choice pop-up.** Keep the existing nine panes and their order; do not invent category mergers without their contents. The persistent label is **Preferences pane:**; the closed chooser displays the selected pane'"'s name and the open menu marks that same choice. Use nine distinct, short, content-predictive noun phrases in title case. Remove duplicate icons; text is required, icons are optional. Do not ship numeric placeholders. The actual names are a content dependency, not evidence of a completed naming exercise. This is pane navigation within one preferences window, not app-level tab-bar navigation. Apple advises avoiding more than six tabs and evaluating another presentation already at six; a pop-up is the selected alternative here, accepting two activations in exchange for fitting nine choices. [Tab views — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-views#Best-practices), [Pop-up buttons — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pop-up-buttons#Best-practices).
2. **Navigation has no save side effects.** Choosing a pane changes only selection, title, and visible content. It never saves documents, unrelated files, or preferences, and never commits a field as a side effect of losing focus. Pane controls affect only their documented settings scope. If an existing control affects another pane, relocate it to the pane owning that effect, or identify a shared app-wide setting explicitly; do not duplicate independently editable values. The navigation prohibition and ownership contract implement Apple's self-contained-pane guidance. [Tab views — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-views#Best-practices).
3. **Keep the frame stable during pane changes.** Reuse one window; preserve its frame, top-left origin, and Close position across every selection, including panes with errors. Keep the chooser above the content, visible and inset within window-body margins. Fit larger content inside the body without automatic window growth; error text consumes body space rather than moving the frame. Choose initial dimensions from measured content and available display area, not invented universal pixel values. All content and correction paths must remain reachable at the smallest supported window size. This fixed-on-switch policy is a product decision addressing the reported failure. [Tab views — Anatomy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-views#Anatomy), [Windows — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/windows#Best-practices).
4. **Preserve useful pane state.** Store selection, each pane's draft values, error details, focus target, and content position for the current app session. Closing hides the window and preserves drafts; reopening restores them and the last pane. Restart restores the last pane and committed preferences only. Explain near an uncommitted field: “Not applied. Press Return to apply a valid value. Unapplied edits are kept until you quit.” No silent normalization or loss on switching. These persistence and draft choices are explicit product policy, not guaranteed framework behavior. [Settings — macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings#macOS).
5. **Handle validation locally without trapping navigation.** Keep raw text while editing, including harmless intermediate values. Show a field-associated explanation identifying the constraint and correction once an invalid complete value is evaluated. Keep the previous committed value active. Return explicitly requests validation and commitment for that field or declared atomic field group; invalid input produces no write and stays available for correction. Escape while editing restores the last committed field/group value and clears its error. Switching panes remains allowed; reopening the pane restores its invalid draft and explanation. Validate again before commitment. Persist only the owned setting, and report persistence failure locally while retaining the draft and previous committed value. The Return/Escape policy is a proposed interaction contract; actual constraints and atomic groups require the missing option inventory. [Entering data — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/entering-data#Best-practices).

## State and transition contract

Each pane has a stable ID, unique display name, ordered fields, ownership mapping, and per-field constraints. Each setting declares app-wide or document-local scope before implementation. App preferences must not mutate open documents; document configuration should be separated from app preferences. Existing defaults remain unchanged pending an inventory; do not invent new defaults or system-preference overrides. [Settings — General settings and Task-specific options](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings#General-settings).

"'```text
state = {selectedPane, windowFrame, panes[id], committedSettings}
panes[id] = {drafts, errors, lastFocus, contentPosition}

selectPane(id):
    require id is one of the nine pane IDs
    if id == selectedPane: return                // no reset or write
    capture current pane'"'s transient state       // navigation never commits
    selectedPane = id
    show retained state for id
    chooser.value = id; window.title = pane[id].displayName
    keep windowFrame unchanged
    keep focus on chooser                        // no surprise jump into content

edit(field, rawValue):
    retain rawValue in owning pane's draft
    evaluate only when meaningful; preserve intermediate entry
    do not write settings or documents

explicitCommit(fieldOrAtomicGroup):
    validate draft against declared constraints
    if invalid: show associated correction; keep committed value; return
    persist only declared setting keys
    if persistence succeeds: update committed values; clear draft errors
    otherwise: retain draft; show failure; keep previous active values

closeWindow(): hide; retain session drafts and pane state; do not commit
reopenWindow(): reuse same window; restore selected pane and session state
restart(): restore last pane ID if available, otherwise first pane;
           load committed values; do not restore session-only drafts
"'```

Chooser opening and cancellation leave selection unchanged. Committing a menu choice closes the menu and shows that pane; repeated selection is a no-op. The menu contains selections only, no Save or other commands, no Custom option, and no submenus. If restored selection no longer exists after a future version change, use the first available pane and update both title and chooser consistently. Longer localized labels must remain distinguishable in the open menu and selected display; widen or reflow the surrounding layout rather than reverting to icons.

Retain system window frame, movement, Close, and activation cues where the host supports them.
